title: Benchmark orchestration and noise modeling for embedding + rerank accuracy
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build an end-to-end evaluation harness that emphasizes realistic perturbations, latency-aware reranker interactions, and an operational 'goldbank' of curated query-candidate pairs. Current embedding checks are unitary (corpus-level similarity distributions) and miss downstream reranker sensitivity and latency trade-offs. This ticket scopes: (1) a goldbank curation workflow with stratified sampling across customers/verticals, (2) a synthetic noise generator that models typo/utterance-shift/formatting and retrieval churn, (3) an offline scoring pipeline that computes rerank-aware metrics (MRR@k, NDCG@k, top-k stability under noise), and (4) drift monitoring signals and alerting thresholds integrated into Console telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Goldbank: a stored corpus of at least 15k human-annotated query-candidate triples covering at least 6 verticals with annotation schema and inter-annotator agreement >= 0.78
Synthetic noise generator: configurable pipeline that can apply at least 5 perturbation classes (typos, paraphrase, truncation, domain-shift, tokenization edge-cases) and is re-usable in CI
Offline metrics: nightly job producing MRR@1/5/10, NDCG@5/10, top-k rank stability, and embedding-similarity calibration plots; outputs pushed to Grafana and persisted to S3

Latency-aware evaluation: end-to-end runner that records batching effects and reranker latency impact for each model/config combination (per-token and end-to-end P50/P95) and compares against baseline SLOs
Drift monitoring: alert rules in Grafana/CloudWatch that fire when top-k stability drops by >6% or MRR falls by >4% relative to 7-day baseline
Runbook: documented triage playbook with reproducible steps and a canary plan to validate mitigations on 1% traffic before rollout
implementation_notes: Goldbank design: store exemplar triples with metadata tags (customer_vertical, org_size_bucket, language, retrieval_context) and link to original document IDs. Use S3 + parquet for storage and a small PostgreSQL index for sampling queries.
Annotation flow: use an annotation UI (internal) with 3 annotators per triple and a reconciliation step. Exported annotations MUST include justification text for borderline cases.
Noise modeling: implement a generator library that outputs both 'token-level' and 'semantic' perturbations. Include seed control for reproducibility in CI runs.

Runner architecture: runner spins up a batched retrieval stage (configurable batch sizes) followed by the reranker variant. Instrument KV-cache hit/miss and measure latency with and without cache warming.
Storage & lineage: each run writes full input/output traces (sampled 0.5%) and summary metrics. Tag runs by model-version, quantization profile, and routing policy.
Operational constraints: nightly job must complete within maintenance window (4h). For longer runs, emit progressive summaries every 30 minutes.
Privacy: sampled traces must be scrubbed (PII masking). Maintain an allowlist of fields preserved for debugging.
test_plan: Unit tests for noise generator covering each perturbation class and reproducibility via seeds
Integration test against a mock reranker that verifies metric computation and storage schema
Canary nightly run: run goldbank job against a subset (10%) of goldbank and validate metrics match local ground truth within tolerance
Load test: simulate 10k queries in parallel to validate batching and ensure end-to-end job remains within maintenance window
SLO regression gate: any change that reduces MRR@5 by >2% in pre-merge CI must block the PR
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal dry-run against historical datasets and record baseline metrics (owner: DataQA)
Phase 2: enable nightly job in staging and add Grafana panels (owner: Observability)
Phase 3: run canary on production traffic (1% of requests) with auto-fallback to previous reranker if alert fires
Phase 4: full rollout with weekly monitoring for 4 weeks and post-mortem if any alert triggers
